result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick an inset low-contrast 1px divider and support it with sound reasoning about density and scanning, along with tabular figures and right-aligned amounts. A goes further on the downsides of both alternatives (zebra stripes clash with pressed and selected states, date headers and dark mode; spacing makes rows look like cards) and gives more concrete values: row height, internal padding, tap target and line placement. B is tighter and adds useful advice on when to choose each alternative, but its only specific values are the contrast percentage and the minimum row height. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers choose an inset 1px divider and justify it well in terms of density and scanning, with tabular figures and right-aligned amounts. B explains the downsides of both alternatives more fully: spacing either takes up too much room or is too small to group rows, and zebra stripes clash with dark mode, accessibility settings, pressed or selected states, and date headers. B also gives more concrete layout values (56–64px rows, 12–16px padding). A gives a contrast range of 8–12%, which B lacks, but B's sizing guidance is more complete overall.
